scope: Requirements-only rendering/provenance addendum for the admitted Parker 1852 quoted circular witness and its single scoped Darwin reply. No converter, transcript, training, export, ledger, or accepted-evidence change.

requirements.case: Quoted Parker circular witness and one cumulative direct reply
requirements.requirement: Represent the supplemental witness explicitly as the attributed John William Parker circular question, not as a new DCP catalogue letter. Preserve the question endpoint at the first final question mark inside the teiquote and exclude the subsequent editorial Campbell paragraph. Link it once to DCP-LETT-1480A, with the reply scope limited to Darwin body paragraph 1; do not mutate the ordinary 1851–1855 period target count.

exact_source_evidence.quote: If a retail Bookseller of ascertained credit and respectability applies to the Publisher to purchase any Book in which you may be directly or indirectly interested, on the terms at which those Books are offered to the Trade at large, but with the avowed intention of retailing his purchases at a smaller profit than that provided for between the wholesale rate and the selling price of single copies,— Do you consider the intention to sell at a low rate of profit, a good and sufficient reason why the Publisher should refuse to sell the Books, which such retailer is ready to purchase and to keep in stock at his own risk?
exact_source_evidence.endpoint_rule: Stop at the question mark after “his own risk?”; the remaining teiquote is modern editorial context about the 19 May Campbell adjudication.
exact_source_evidence.normalization: Whitespace only; preserve source capitalization and punctuation.

exact_source_evidence.quote: As an author of some Scientific works, I beg to express strongly my opinion, that, both for the advantage of Authors & the public, Booksellers like other dealers ought to settle, each for himself, the Retail price.
exact_source_evidence.response_scope: Only this retained Darwin P1 answer is linked to the circular question.

date_voice_receipt_requirements: Keep Parker’s 30 April 1852 date as circular composition/stated date; original physical circular and complete salutation/introduction remain unavailable.

Keep DCP-LETT-1480A as Darwin to John William Parker, 5 May [1852], with supplied year retained. This establishes a reply date and at most known-by date 5 May; it does not establish actual receipt or reading date for Parker’s circular.

Preserve authored Darwin first-person prose above. Do not render or cite the DCP Summary sentence “As an author of some scientific works CD is of the opinion...” as Darwin body evidence; it is a third-person editorial summary.
Do not infer a separate incoming Parker-to-Darwin catalogue record or physical delivery from the embedded quotation.

requirements.requirement: Use the Mill edition only as corroboration: Parker question is quoted inside a modern editorial headnote, while Dear Sir begins Mill own answer dated May8 in the headnote and signed J. S. Mill. The headnote framing and Mill reply are neither Darwin voice nor Darwin prior knowledge. The embedded Parker wording corroborates the admitted prompt excerpt; the DCP quotation supplies its selected text/version. No original Parker-to-Darwin physical copy is thereby recovered.
